purpose: Beacon frames — the policy advertisement (SSID, RSNE, WPS, capabilities).
Probe responses — reveals hidden SSIDs and per-client capabilities.
Probe requests — client intent / preferred network list leakage.
Authentication frames — algorithm and status codes.
Association request / response — negotiated policy and status codes.
Deauthentication — reason codes, source, timing.
Disassociation — reason codes (e.g. 8 = STA leaving).
All management frames — a useful overview filter.
Beacons/frames carrying the RSN information element (element 48).
SAE (WPA3-Personal) AKM present.
802.1X (enterprise) AKM present.
PSK AKM present — in a WPA3 deployment this indicates transition mode.
PMF capable (MFPC bit set).
PMF required (MFPR bit set) — spoofed deauth should fail.
Vendor-specific IEs, including WPS (OUI 00:50:F2).
WPS registrar is in setup-locked state.
All EAPOL frames (EAP authentication and 4-way handshake).
EAPOL-Key frames — the 4-way handshake (M1–M4).
M2/M4-style MIC-flagged key frames (verify with key_info, not order).
All EAP frames — method identification, identity exchange.
PEAP (EAP type 25); type 13 = EAP-TLS, 21 = EAP-TTLS, 26 = MS-CHAPv2, 254 = WSC.
RADIUS traffic (authentication/accounting) visible on the capture path.
RADIUS Access-Challenge — the server is driving an EAP exchange.
Dynamic VLAN/group assignment attribute in an Access-Accept.
Protected (encrypted) data frames — payload not readable without the PTK.
Unprotected data frames — cleartext payload (often an open/WEP BSS).
One BSS — the right granularity for a finding.
ICMP — the reachability evidence for isolation/segmentation tests.
DHCP — lease source, which exposes a rogue network quickly.
HTTP methods/hosts/URIs — portal flows and cleartext credentials.
